title: Micro-magnetic resonance imaging of ex vivo mouse embryos with potato starch suspension
protocol: Prepare paraformaldehyde (PFA) and phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dissolve 1 piece of PBS tablets and 1 mL sodium azide into 999 mL distilled water.
If a contrast agent is required, dissolve 10 mL Gadoteridol (Gd), 1 piece of PBS tablets, and 1 mL sodium azide into 989 mL PBS to create Gd-PBS.
Dissolve 10 mL of Gd into 990 mL paraformaldehyde to create Gd-PFA.
Place PFA and Gd-PFA in the refrigerator to cool them at 4°C.
Euthanize pregnant mice by cervical dislocation.
Wipe the euthanized mouse with ethanol.
Open the abdomen with scissors.
Remove the embryo and place it on a petri dish containing PBS.
Wash the embryo with PBS.
Transfer the embryo to a fresh dish containing PBS.
Wash the removed embryo in PBS.
Transfer the embryo into 4% PFA.
Store the embryo at 4°C for at least 1 day.
Move the specimens to PBS or Gd-PBS after fixation.
Store the fixed specimens at 4°C.
Put naturally died wasp from winter into PFA or Gd-PFA.
Store the solution in the refrigerator at 4°C until needed.
Transfer the fixed wasp specimens into PBS or Gd-PBS.
Make PS-PBS solution.
Prepare 7.25 g of potato starch powder and 5 mL PBS (or Gd-PBS if a contrast agent is required) at room temperature.
Gradually add the potato starch powder to the PBS or Gd-PBS.
Wait 10 seconds after adding the powder.
Mix the mixture thoroughly with a Pasteur pipette.
Place the specimen into the PS-PBS solution tube.
Mix the potato starch and PBS with a Pasteur pipette.
Tilt the tube and add the PS-PBS or Gd-PS-PBS into the tube little by little with a Pasteur pipette.
Remove supernatant PBS or Gd-PBS with a Pasteur pipette.
Wait for 10–30 min until the PS sinks to the bottom completely.
Confirm that the specimen is within the PS and it does not move by eyes.
Set the tube into the MRI magnet.
Mark the right position, which is the center of the magnetic field, with magic pen.
Put the tube at the right position in the radio frequency coil.
Immobilize the tube tightly with tape and sponges.
Place the MRI bed into the MR bore.
Adjust the tuning and matching under the wobble mode.
Start the tripilot sequence to adjust field homogeneity, shimming, and reference pulse gain automatically.
Scan T1-weighted or T2-weighted images of mouse embryo or wasp.

Scan a T1-weighted image of the mouse embryo using 3D-fast low angle shot (FLASH) with parameters: TE/TR = 6/60 ms, flip angle = 90 degree, FOV = 15 × 15 × 10 mm³, matrix = 512 × 512 × 200, resolution = 29 × 29 × 20 μm³/voxel, Average = 20, total scan time = 11 h 22 min.
Scan T2-weighted image of the mouse embryo using rapid acquisition with relaxation enhancement (RARE).
Remove the specimen from PS suspension.
Mix the deposited potato starch with a Pasteur pipette.
Check that the specimen floats.
Remove the PS suspension by a Pasteur pipette.
Gently pick up the sample with tweezers and pull it out of the solution.
Wash the specimen with PBS.
Transfer the specimen into PBS or Gd-PBS.
